diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call a triple of pure quaternions $(\unitp,\unitq,\unitr)$ orthonormal if and only if  $\unitp,\unitq,\unitr$ are all units and any two of them are orthogonal.

issues.failure_explanation: Orthogonality and unit length do not determine orientation. For example, $(\unitp,\unitq,\unitr)=(\uniti,\unitj,-\unitk)$ satisfies Definition \ref{orthogonalunitsdef}, but $\unitp\unitq=\unitk=-\unitr$. Consequently the displayed decomposition of $A$ and the formal assertion in Lemma \ref{orthonormalunitlm0}(i) are false for an allowed triple. The complexification and subsequent coordinate calculations assume the missing relation $\unitp\unitq=\unitr$.

failure_location.quote: Any orthonormal triple of pure quaternions $(\unitp,\unitq,\unitr)$ can be treated as a three-axis imaginary system like $(\uniti,\unitj,\unitk)$, see Property 1 in \cite{pan2024block}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the triple to be positively oriented, for example by adding $\unitp\unitq=\unitr$ to Definition \ref{orthogonalunitsdef}, and consistently restrict all subsequent coordinate constructions to such triples.
issues.overall_effect: The quaternion-to-complex representation and the generating-function, spectral, preconditioning, and convergence arguments are not established for every orthonormal triple permitted by the paper's definition.
issues.title: Orthonormal imaginary triples need not have the assumed quaternion orientation
issues.why_classification: A standard local orientation condition restores the algebra used throughout without changing the substantive spectral conclusions, rates, or algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed symbol, the adjoint of the upper-right entry $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ is $-\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$, whereas the lower-left entry is $+\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$. Thus $G[f](x)$ is generally not Hermitian. Moreover, the quadratic-form calculation immediately preceding the conclusion uses $+\phi_2(f)(x)$ in the upper-right position, so it does not equal the stated $G[f]$ quadratic form. Courant–Fischer is therefore applied to the wrong, non-Hermitian symbol.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct one off-diagonal sign, together with the corresponding term in the quadratic-form calculation, so that the two off-diagonal entries are conjugates; then propagate that consistent convention through later occurrences of $G[f]$.
issues.overall_effect: The Rayleigh identity and its proof are false as written, and later spectral arguments invoking the Hermitian symbol are unsupported until its off-diagonal signs are made consistent.
issues.title: The matrix-valued symbol G[f] is not Hermitian
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local sign inconsistency. Either consistent Hermitian sign convention has the same symbol eigenvalues because those depend on $|\phi_2(f)|$, so the advertised bounds and rates can be retained.

issues.failure_explanation: When $n$ is even, $m=n/2$, but the Strang first column explicitly sets the lag-$m$ coefficient to zero. The stated $f_m$ instead includes both $\eta(m)e^{\unitp mx}$ and its conjugate term. At the Fourier grid these terms generally contribute rather than vanish, so the claimed exact eigenvalue formula does not describe the defined preconditioner.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the truncation through $m-1$ when $n$ is even, or define a parity-dependent truncated symbol whose lag-$n/2$ coefficient is zero. The omitted tail coefficient tends to zero under absolute summability, so the limiting statement can then be reproved unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma \ref{strangcireiglimitlm}(i) is false for even $n$, and the later asymptotic preconditioner arguments rely on an incorrect exact diagonalization formula.
issues.title: The exact Strang spectrum uses the wrong truncation for even dimensions
issues.why_classification: A local parity-dependent truncation correction restores the exact formula and leaves the asymptotic limits, clustering, and convergence rate unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\beta$ is a given quaternion parameter with $|\beta|\in(0,1)$;

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis permits nonzero real $\beta$, for which $\beta_I=0$. Then ${\bf m}=\beta_I/|\beta_I|$ and several subsequent formulas containing $|\beta_I|^{-1}$ are undefined. The derivation therefore does not cover the full parameter range stated in the example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the local hypothesis $\beta_I\ne0$ to the displayed derivation and treat real $\beta$ separately using the scalar formulas, or provide the corresponding limiting expressions.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed polar decomposition and generating-function formulas in Example \ref{ar1} are not well defined for real AR parameters, despite those parameters satisfying the stated assumptions.
issues.title: The AR(1) formulas are undefined for allowed real parameters
issues.why_classification: The excluded degenerate case has an elementary separate treatment and does not alter the model, positivity conclusion, or subsequent convergence theory.
